s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal cystic mass with calcifications and mural nodularity in a patient with a history of breast cancer
salient_findings: Complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head
Enhancing septa, millimetric nodules, and soft-tissue components
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
History of left breast cancer
Treated by modified radical mastectomy and axillary dissection two years earlier
Asymptomatic
Physical examination and laboratory studies within normal limits
Serum tumor markers within normal limits
Abdominal ultrasonography showed a complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a cystic lesion in the uncinate process
Calcifications, enhancing septa, millimetric nodules, and soft-tissue components present
No distant metastases or intraabdominal lymphadenopathy
ASA-2 anesthetic evaluation

shortlist.label: Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head with calcifications and mural nodularity

shortlist.label: Mucinous Cystic Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic lesion in the uncinate process with calcifications, enhancing septa, and soft-tissue components

shortlist.label: Pancreatic Metastasis from Breast Cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of left breast cancer and presence of a complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head

shortlist.label: Cystic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic lesion in the uncinate process with calcifications and soft-tissue components, concerning for malignancy

shortlist.label: Solid Pseudopapillary Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic lesion with calcifications, enhancing septa, and soft-tissue components, characteristic of this tumor type

raw.rationale: The presence of a complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head with internal calcifications, mural nodularity, and enhancing septa is more characteristic of a Mucinous Cystic Neoplasm, which often presents with these imaging features and is more common in women.

rejected.label: Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm
rejected.why: IPMNs typically involve the main pancreatic duct or its branches and are less likely to present as a complex cystic mass with calcifications.

rejected.label: Pancreatic Metastasis from Breast Cancer
rejected.why: There is no evidence of distant metastases, and the primary breast cancer was treated two years earlier, making a metastasis less likely.

rejected.label: Cystic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the absence of lymphadenopathy and distant metastases, along with the specific imaging characteristics, makes this less likely than a Mucinous Cystic Neoplasm.

rejected.label: Solid Pseudopapillary Neoplasm
rejected.why: SPN typically occurs in younger women and has a more solid appearance on imaging, which does not match the complex cystic mass described in this case.
